text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any specific physical anomalies, such as a rash, respiratory distress, or congenital malformations, observed on this newborn? Please also describe the mother's health during pregnancy and any known infections or exposures.

text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: This constellation of findings—patent ductus arteriosus, congenital cataracts, and sensorineural hearing loss—is highly suggestive of Congenital Rubella Syndrome. Did the mother experience any rash, fever, or arthritis during the first trimester of pregnancy?

text: Past medical history: Newborn, no past medical history available. Social history: Mother is a primigravida, no prenatal care received.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the lack of prenatal care and the classic triad of findings, I suspect Congenital Rubella Syndrome. To confirm this, I will order specific serological testing for rubella antibodies in both the infant and the mother. REQUEST TEST: Rubella IgG and IgM
